quarterly_data.signal: SHORT-DATED CAPEX IS A FILL-RATE ESTIMATE (the >50% dock-to-live improvement itself was already disclosed on the Q4 FY2026 earnings call; new here is the fill-rate framing of short-dated capex): CFO Amy Hood said the efficiency work now runs 'almost at the shovel layer' - the teams cut the time from bringing a data center online to a piece of hardware being 'revenue ready', reducing 'dock-to-live times over the course of a year by more than 50%', with the improvement concentrated in H2. Short-dated capex is therefore a fill-rate estimate: the priority right now is 'how quickly we can get supply revenue ready', not moving a billion dollars of capex between sites, because very little new capacity can be built and come online within 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: dock-to-live times over the course of a year by more than 50%

quarterly_data.signal: SUPPLY-CHAIN LOCK-UP: Hood said Microsoft has signed long-term agreements (LTAs) 'with a lot of the supply chain' to secure full 'matching sets' of the kit needed for a data center rather than one component, and that a lot of work and significant investment went into this over the past 12 months - a point she said the market had not fully appreciated, that it is the whole set of components and not just one piece that has to be secured.
